status: The final client candidate is measured alongside published Forma and pre-effect main. Public effects improve substantially; the original fan-out and row-creation targets remain missed, with batching and DOM point regressions disclosed below. These limitations are accepted as prospective 3.1 product tradeoffs. Packed release qualification, publication and burn-in are not established by this report.
method: Fresh Linux campaigns use separately recorded VM identities and the dated gha-4-v1 allocation. Compare trials only within a campaign; all samples, spreads and earlier failed outcomes are retained. Historical October 23 standings remain in the separate historical report.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — Linux protocol and evidence boundaries
sections.description: Round 2 uses the dated gha-4-v1 profile on standard GitHub Actions Linux VMs with four available vCPUs. This profile preserves complete sample counts and separates server and load-generator CPUs; it does not claim an exclusive physical host.
rows: Sequential own-engine control in the same campaign
sections.note: Each campaign records source and lock hashes, actual container limits, CPU affinity, browser hashes where applicable, smoke checks and cleanup. Earlier oversubscribed runs remain diagnostic. Only trials in the same campaign support before/after ratios. The original October 23 results remain in the separate historical report.

sections.title: Final client campaign — measured outcome and release decision
sections.description: Run 40140319634 measures published 3.0.0, pre-effect main f5be8647 and final integrated candidate 9ac07a44 sequentially on one Linux VM. Each workload retains two warmups and five measured samples. The full source IDs, original ZIP, own-engine controls and raw samples accompany this report. Row profiling was disabled.
sections.note: The original fan-out and row-creation targets are still missed. Write, effect creation/disposal and the overall signal ratio meet their individual numerical targets in this campaign. The maintainer accepted the remaining misses as explicit 3.1 product tradeoffs while retaining default row and native listener semantics; no experimental compiler is included. This prospective decision does not turn failed historical targets into passes, establish packed qualification, publish an RC or satisfy burn-in.

sections.title: Final client campaign — all nine reactive-core workloads
sections.description: Values are millions of operations per second, mean ± sample SD; higher is better. The last column divides final Forma mean throughput by its contemporaneous pristine alien-signals 3.1.2 mean, which matches Forma’s own engine dependency. The separate official alien-signals race entry is 3.2.1.
sections.note: Final writes improve 70.74%, fan-out 145.77% and effect creation/disposal 251.34% versus published Forma in this campaign. The batch-of-100-writes mean regresses 13.79% versus published and 6.93% versus pre-effect main. All five samples and their substantial spreads remain visible in the evidence; overlapping SDs do not prove equivalence. The 86.62% overall own-engine ratio does not erase that batching point regression or the 71.64% fan-out miss.

sections.title: Final client campaign — all nine DOM operations
sections.description: Milliseconds, mean ± sample SD; lower is better. Each source has its own same-trial vanilla control in the archive; the table shows the final candidate’s paired vanilla. Percentage changes compare the final candidate with published and pre-effect main in this same campaign.
sections.note: Create-1,000 is 44.56 ± 4.11 ms versus vanilla 26.14 ± 2.40 ms: 1.705×, above the original 1.10× target. Selection is 1.36 ms versus published 0.68 ms, though pre-effect main is already 1.58 ms. Clear rises from main’s 4.60 ms to 6.00 ms (+30.43%), with published at 6.04 ms. These point regressions are disclosed, not hidden by a geometric mean. Five sequential samples and nonrandomized source order limit causal attribution; no blanket non-regression claim is made.

sections.title: Final client campaign — application bytes and evidence boundaries
sections.description: All statically loaded JavaScript for the unchanged client benchmark application. These bytes belong to each source in run 40140319634; they are separate from package import-graph and island-route budgets.
sections.note: The final application is 8,498 B Brotli: 154 B smaller than published Forma and 81 B larger than pre-effect main. The independent package/route size decisions, their old-limit misses and their new ceilings are documented separately. This campaign uses gha-4-v1: signal processes receive one CPU/1 GiB on CPU 0, and the browser/driver use CPUs 1–3 with the locked Chromium 156.0.8078.4. No cross-campaign timing gains, final server rerace, publication or deployment are inferred.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — qualified fourteen-server championship
sections.description: The corrected full Linux campaign independently passes source, resource, transport and score replay checks. It measures published Forma 3.0.0 and thirteen other server entrants on one VM, under the frozen gha-4-v1 profile. This is a server-only baseline.
sections.note: The unchanged points schedule is 25,18,15,12,10,8,6,4,2,1; ties share occupied positions. Event 7 splits its points equally between image and gzip-response weight. Forma ranks 7 of 14 with 59.5 points, first in memory and image size and second in Grid start. No client or overall-combined ranking is inferred. Earlier unresolved server results remain archived separately.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — all server HTTP measurements
sections.description: Three ten-second samples per event follow five-second warmups. Values are mean ± sample SD. Single-core events use one server CPU; multicore uses two; the two-CPU driver has disjoint affinity.
sections.note: All 168 timed loads, 56 warmups, 112 probe bodies and 294 transport records are retained. Probes and loads share explicit headers. Each identity aggregate equals the verified probe length multiplied by completed responses, including React Router. This validates aggregate representation length with sampled semantic checks; it does not prove every individual timed response. Compare absolute timings only within this campaign.

sources.label: Full raw HTTP and transport evidence

sections.title: FORMA-264 — all server resource and build measurements
sections.description: Memory, Grid start and build cells show mean ± sample SD. Image and gzip-response sizes are byte measurements. Grid start includes the Docker command; builds are warm page-only release builds under the recorded four-CPU build allocation.
sections.note: Forma passes the separate strength budgets: mean memory peak 4.033333 MiB ≤8, readiness remainder after docker run returns 18.144030 ms ≤50, and image 78,187,609 B ≤150,000,000. The boot remainder is not pure process startup; the scored Grid event is 178.014610 ms. A separate same-executable distroless check saves 47,156,656 B with body/policy parity; it establishes image size and correctness only.

sources.label: Resource, build and separate runtime evidence

sections.title: FORMA-257 and FORMA-258 — same-runner server comparison
sections.description: Published 3.0.0 → walker-only be029708 → static-only d00f231a → combined 81d1fd81. Three 10-second samples after 5-second warmups on one Linux VM. Values show mean ± sample SD; multicore uses two CPUs.
sections.note: Static output is 48.32% smaller and passes the 17,500 B target. Combined Sprint improves 3.74%; Endurance changes −0.10%. The estimated 3,300/5,000 req/s did not materialize. The historical tail rule is mean p99 divided by mean p50; all four pass ≤1.5. Walker-only sample 3 individually reached 1.5264 and is retained. Sequential order and three samples limit causal attribution.

sections.title: FORMA-258 — walker cost and unchanged work
sections.description: A separate post-race instrumented executable reports existing RenderCounts; the raced binary is unchanged. Twenty warmups precede 101 measurements at each row count. The original binary and all document bodies are authenticated.
sections.note: All reported walker mean costs are below 10 ns/B; individual samples and spread remain in the raw evidence. This is not the HTTP marginal-cost metric: HTTP also includes data preparation, projection, response construction and transport. Static mode removes output bytes while retaining all nodes/list iterations, so ns per output byte can rise while total work falls. Separate macOS allocation counts were 1,937→1,133 at 100 rows and 19,044→11,040 at 1,000; those counts are not Linux measurements.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — server budgets and runtime image experiment
sections.description: All four trials pass unchanged memory ≤8 MiB, application boot ≤50 ms and image ≤150,000,000 B budgets. Every individual memory/boot observation also passes.
sections.note: Memory is the mean of observed per-run peaks. The readiness remainder runs from the Docker command returning until the first HTTP 200; it is not pure process startup. The pinned distroless image saves 47,156,656 B using the identical executable, runs as UID 65532 and passes 10/100/1,000-row body/policy parity. This is a size/correctness experiment; no distroless throughput, memory or boot claim, and no default image change.

sections.title: FORMA-261 — optional response compression
sections.description: Same executable and runner, three 10-second samples after 5-second warmups. Source 87ecea92 includes the walker improvement and precedes static-route suppression. These are compression costs, not final-release or published-baseline speedups.
sections.note: Brotli saves 92.5% of bytes with 26.0% lower Sprint throughput and 34.2% higher p99. gzip saves 91.6% with 29.0% lower throughput and 42.4% higher p99. Compression remains off by default; opt in only after the response-specific BREACH decision. Decoded content, response policy, resources and cleanup passed.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — eleven native island implementations
sections.description: Published Forma 3.0.0 baseline. Each car passed one JavaScript-disabled SSR check, two warmups and five fresh measured contexts. All 154 counter increments, server-rendered counter-node identity and 100-row content checks passed. Timing cells show median (minimum–maximum) in milliseconds, as specified by the island protocol.
sections.note: Ready runs from navigation start to the framework hook. Activation spans differ by native framework API; Next and Astro have no comparable explicit start. JS transfer includes HTTP overhead and is not Brotli bundle size. Click measures programmatic dispatch to matching text, not physical input or paint. Row content is verified; row-node identity is not measured. This baseline makes no candidate speedup claim.

sections.title: FORMA-259, FORMA-260 and FORMA-263 — retained failed client trial
sections.description: The first qualified Linux comparison tested published 3.0.0 against candidate 54a836c0. It exposed DOM regressions. The row optimizations were withdrawn; a subsequent three-trial comparison tested the published version, this failed candidate and rollback 16862984.
rows: Within 10% of paired vanilla 21.66 ms: failed

The official signal comparator was alien-signals 3.2.1; it cannot establish the target against Forma’s own 3.1.2 dependency. The successor campaign adds that exact control. No favorable-run selection or pooling across campaigns.

sections.title: FORMA-259 and FORMA-263 — verified rollback comparison
sections.description: One new Linux campaign tests published 3.0.0, withdrawn candidate 54a836c0 and rollback 16862984 sequentially, with five samples after two warmups. The exact alien-signals 3.1.2 control runs separately in each trial under the same resource profile.
rows: write with one effect / own engine
effect create and dispose / own engine
sections.note: The rollback saves 228 B Brotli versus published 3.0.0 (2.64%), leaving a 356 B gap to Preact. The three effect targets of at least 80% each and overall target of at least 85% remain unmet. This VM has a different CPU model from the original campaign; absolute timings must not be compared across the two runs.

sections.title: FORMA-260 — all nine DOM operations after rollback
sections.description: All measurements are milliseconds, mean ± sample SD. The last column retains each trial’s contemporaneous vanilla baseline. Creation remains above the required 1.10× vanilla limit.
sections.note: Rollback create-1,000 is 47.74 ms versus 28.34 ms for vanilla, a 1.685× ratio. No rollback-versus-published mean increase exceeds the sum of their observed SDs, but that descriptive check does not prove equivalence. Baseline drift and clock-resolution effects remain visible. The rollback does not establish which earlier optimization caused the regressions or close the row-creation ticket.

sections.title: FORMA-262 — release-build caching
sections.description: One cold/warm pair per authenticated published starter on separate hosted runners. The warm run edits a page, restores the exact reviewed cache and rebuilds no registry artifacts. Each cold run reports 113 registry compilation artifacts across 89 unique package IDs.
sections.note: These are measured starter examples, not universal build-time guarantees. The shipped CI cache policy is read-only outside the default branch. Release loading of FMIR from disk remains deferred after evaluating authentication, atomic updates and version skew; development already reloads pages from disk.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — retained unresolved server campaign
sections.description: The first 14-stack Linux workflow completed, but each of its 12 React Router load samples reported a floored mean response size 660 bytes shorter than its separate smoke response: 30,473 vs 31,133 bytes at 100 rows, and 276,112 vs 276,772 at 1,000 rows.
rows: Source, resource allocation, coverage and cleanup
All 168 retained; 12 React Router response-length mismatches
All 156 timed lengths match the corresponding probes
Unresolved; not promoted into the round 2 leaderboard
sections.note: The load generator and Node probes sent different user agents. React Router can choose different streaming behavior for bots, but timed response bodies were not retained, so that explanation cannot retrospectively establish equivalence. A new full campaign fixes explicit user-agent, Accept and encoding headers, retains exact probes and raw load output, and refuses identity-body length differences. No framework bytes are normalized and no results are spliced across VMs.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — seven-client Linux baseline
sections.description: The published-source trial of the first qualified client campaign, selected as the baseline independently of its timings. Five measured samples follow two warmups. Bundle values are all statically loaded application JavaScript; create-1,000 values are milliseconds, mean ± sample SD.
sections.note: All nine operation samples are retained in the original archive. Each later candidate trial has its own contemporaneous vanilla measurement; do not substitute this baseline for those paired controls. These figures do not change the separate historical leaderboard.

sections.title: FORMA-264 — five reactive-core Linux baselines
sections.description: Published-source trial from the same first client campaign. Each reactive-core process runs alone in its recorded one-CPU/1-GiB container. Values are millions of operations per second, mean ± sample SD across five samples after two warmups; higher is better.
sections.note: Work differs across benchmark rows, so compare libraries within a row. Large spreads are retained. The official alien-signals entry is 3.2.1; the later effect-acceptance comparison separately pins Forma’s own 3.1.2 engine. They are different controls.

sections.title: FORMA-263 — independently extracted bundle change
sections.description: A separate bundle-only change at 8b56026e excludes the effect optimization and all withdrawn row optimizations. Fresh local production builds use identical app sources, external dependencies and Node 24.22.0 / Vite 8.3.5.
sections.note: The isolated change saves 237 B Brotli (2.74%). A separate source-map build shows activation code (666 mapped bytes) and state-encoder setup (16) disappear from this client-only app. Compression savings are not additive by module. All 4,164 unit tests, 42 three-engine checks and existing package/route size limits pass. These are local static byte measurements, not new Linux timings or the earlier combined candidate’s 8,424 B result.
